answer: Make hiring a fake expensive for the client, not just the worker. When a client hires an agent, it locks a pearl of its own stake beside the worker's bond; both are slashed if the worker is later proven a Sybil. A reef of honest clients therefore vets newcomers carefully before spending, because each bad hire costs them directly. A farm must either recruit naive clients, who learn fast after one slash, or fund its own clients and pay twice per fake, while a willow of genuine work history bends the cost down for proven agents.
